BUSINESS DRIVERS
Model business levers

Revenue is calculated from the business drivers. Do not type in a made-up revenue target. Adjust the levers below to test how the model changes.

Select Upside or Downside to edit business driver assumptions.
PRIMARY INTERNAL LEVERS
Productive labour output %% of current productive labour baseline

100% equals your current productive labour baseline. Increase this to test whether more productive output improves recovery without changing your charge-out rate.

Charge-out rate$ per productive hour / contribution hour

Pricing lever. Use this to test whether changing your rate improves or weakens the model.

Margin target %% target margin

Commercial target. This changes the required benchmark, not revenue by itself.

GROWTH LEVER
Billable volume change %% change from baseline volume

Optional. Use this after testing productive labour output, rate, and margin. It models more or less billable work being sold or completed.

Reset Scenario To Baseline

You can combine levers. For example, test whether higher productive labour output allows you to lower charge-out rates while still maintaining recovery.

HOW BUSINESS MODELLING WORKS
Controlled scenario benchmark

Business Summary shows what the business currently is. Business Modelling shows what the business could become if the assumptions change.

Baseline is the locked current business. It is read-only unless you refresh it explicitly from current Business Summary.

Upside tests a stronger performance scenario. Downside tests pressure. Scenario changes do not alter the real business model.

Quote Engine can later test quotes against the selected model, using the benchmark created here.
